expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

emoji.description: The reaction: an emoji's name or the character itself, at most 32 code points.

limit.description: At most this many reactions; 50 when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read who reacted to a message with one emoji, in the order they reacted.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: documents_list_pinned
tools.title: documents: listPinned
tools.description: Lists the conversation's pinned messages, top-level and replies, in ascending id order, one page at a time. Only a posted or interrupted message is pinned: a deleted one loses its pin, and a composing one cannot take one.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many messages; 50 when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read the conversation's pinned messages, top-level and replies, in ascending id order.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items, each a record, and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: documents_list_revisions
tools.title: documents: listRevisions
tools.description: Lists the instance's revisions, oldest first, one page at a time.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many revisions; 50 when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read the instance's revisions, oldest first: each its number and the own fields as that change left them.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not page through them for one revision; call getRevision with its number.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: documents_get_revision
tools.title: documents: getRevision
tools.description: Reads one of the instance's revisions by its number: the own fields as that change left them. A number the instance has not reached is not_found.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read one revision by its number, the one a pinned link or a proposal names say: the own fields as that change left them.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the revision; a number the instance has not reached is not_found.

tools.name: documents_propose
tools.title: documents: propose
tools.description: Proposes a change to the instance's own fields as a JSON merge patch, for a reviewer to approve or reject. The patch must change the instance and leave it valid; nothing changes until a reviewer approves it.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

evidence.description: Instances the proposal cites, for the reviewer: each one must exist and the proposer must be able to read its schema, and a revision must be one it has had, of a schema that composes Revisions. They are kept as given; a later change of an instance cited leaves them as they are.

revision.description: The revision of it the proposal rests on.

schema.description: The schema of the instance cited.

patch.description: A JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) of the instance's own fields.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to propose a change of the own fields, as a JSON merge patch, for a caller with permission documents.review to approve. evidence cites instances the proposer may read, each optionally at a revision it has had.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change the instance at once; call update.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the pending proposal with its id and its evidence; the instance does not change until it is approved.

tools.name: documents_approve
tools.title: documents: approve
tools.description: Approves a pending proposal: applies its patch to the instance as an update, whose checks run, and records the revision it makes. Needs the review permission.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

proposal.description: The id of the pending proposal.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to apply a pending proposal; it needs permission documents.review, else the call is forbidden.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the proposal, approved, with the revision its patch made.

errors.description: Revisions: approve or reject of a proposal that is no longer pending.
errors.commonCorrection: Read the proposal with listProposals: someone has already settled it.

tools.name: documents_reject
tools.title: documents: reject
tools.description: Rejects a pending proposal; the instance does not change. Needs the review permission.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

proposal.description: The id of the pending proposal.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to turn a pending proposal down, with an optional reason; it needs permission documents.review, else the call is forbidden.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the proposal, rejected; the instance does not change.

errors.description: Revisions: approve or reject of a proposal that is no longer pending.
errors.commonCorrection: Read the proposal with listProposals: someone has already settled it.

tools.name: documents_list_proposals
tools.title: documents: listProposals
tools.description: Lists the instance's proposals, oldest first, one page at a time; with state, only those in it.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many proposals; 50 when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read the instance's proposals, oldest first, each with the evidence it cites; with state, only the pending, approved or rejected ones.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.title: Create projects
tools.description: Creates a projects: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Project: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name. A new instance's status is active.

tools.name: projects_get
tools.title: Get projects
tools.description: Returns the projects with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Project to read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Project instances; call list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance with its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: projects_list
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: Lists projects instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

cursor.description: The previous page's next

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

anyOf.description: The state the instance is in.

items.description: The state the instance is in.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Project instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title or Workflow.status; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's. where: { "Workflow.status": <state> } lists the instances in one of active, done or dropped, and a list of states the instances in any of them.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read one instance whose id you have; call get.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null. With where, a page can hold fewer items than limit, even none, while next is not null: read on until it is.

tools.name: projects_update
tools.title: Update projects
tools.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the projects with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Project

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Project with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations. Do not use to move Workflow's status, which behaviors.Workflow holds; call transition.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

tools.name: projects_delete
tools.title: Delete projects
tools.description: Deletes the projects with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Project with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

tools.name: projects_transition
tools.title: projects: transition
tools.description: Moves the instance to another state along a transition the config lists. A transition that names a permission needs a caller who holds it.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to move status from active to done or dropped.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use from done or dropped: no transition leaves a terminal state. Do not use to stay where the instance is. Read behaviors.Rollups.values before a move: a move into done waits until tasksFinished holds.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns from and to; status holds to from then on, and enteredAt the time of the move.

errors.description: Workflow: No transition leads from the instance's status to the state named; details.allowed lists the states it can move to.
errors.commonCorrection: Read status, then name a state details.allowed lists, or move through one of them first.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance is already in the state the transition names.
errors.commonCorrection: Read status: the instance is already there, so nothing needs to move.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance is in a terminal state: no transition leaves it.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the work has ended. Create a new instance to start again.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance has no status to move from.
errors.commonCorrection: None: an instance without a status cannot move.

errors.description: Rollups: A move into a state a rollup gates while the rollup does not hold; details names the rollup and counts the linked instances it read and counted.
errors.commonCorrection: Read behaviors.Rollups.values, and finish the linked work the rollup waits on, then try again.

tools.name: tasks_create
tools.title: Create tasks
tools.description: Creates a tasks: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given. behaviors gives its behaviors their create parameters (Dependencies, Links), which hold from the create on.

behaviors.description: Each behavior's create parameters, by behavior name; they hold from the create on, in its transaction

blockers.description: The instance's blockers from its create, each held to addBlocker's rules: an instance of tasks or documents.

schema.description: The blocker's schema; tasks when absent.

Links.description: The links the instance holds from its create, by name, each held to link's rules.

parent.description: The tasks instance parent points at: its id.

project.description: The projects instance project points at: its id.

spec.description: The documents instance spec points at: its id, or an object with its id and the revision to record, its latest when absent.

revision.description: The target's revision to record, one it has had.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Task: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one. behaviors gives Dependencies and Links their create parameters, which hold from the create on. behaviors.Dependencies.blockers gives the instance its blockers from the create, at most 500, each an instance of tasks or documents (the instance's own schema when schema is absent). behaviors.Links gives the links from the create, by name (parent, project and spec): each the target's id, or { id, revision } for spec. project is required.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name. A new instance's status is todo.

errors.description: Dependencies: addBlocker, or a create's blockers, naming an instance that already blocks this one.
errors.commonCorrection: Leave it: that instance already blocks this one.

errors.description: Dependencies: addBlocker, or a create's blockers, giving an edge that would close a cycle.
errors.commonCorrection: Remove the edge that makes the other instance wait on this one first, or leave this edge out.

errors.description: Dependencies: addBlocker, or a create's blockers, giving an open blocker while the instance is in a gated state no transition leaves.
errors.commonCorrection: Add only finished blockers to an instance in a gated state no transition leaves, or none.

errors.description: Links: A link pinned to a revision, by link or a create's links, to a target that has no revision to pin yet.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait until the target has a revision, or link a target that has one.

tools.name: tasks_get
tools.title: Get tasks
tools.description: Returns the tasks with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Task to read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Task instances; call list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance with its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: tasks_list
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: Lists tasks instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

cursor.description: The previous page's next

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

anyOf.description: The state the instance is in.

items.description: The state the instance is in.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Task instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title or Workflow.status; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's. where: { "Workflow.status": <state> } lists the instances in one of todo, doing, done or dropped, and a list of states the instances in any of them.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read one instance whose id you have; call get.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null. With where, a page can hold fewer items than limit, even none, while next is not null: read on until it is.

tools.name: tasks_update
tools.title: Update tasks
tools.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the tasks with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Task

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Task with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations. Do not use to move Workflow's status, which behaviors.Workflow holds; call transition.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

tools.name: tasks_delete
tools.title: Delete tasks
tools.description: Deletes the tasks with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Task with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

tools.name: tasks_transition
tools.title: tasks: transition
tools.description: Moves the instance to another state along a transition the config lists. A transition that names a permission needs a caller who holds it.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to move status from todo to doing or dropped; from doing to done or dropped.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use from done or dropped: no transition leaves a terminal state. Do not use to stay where the instance is. Do not move into done while blocked is true.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns from and to; status holds to from then on, and enteredAt the time of the move.

errors.description: Workflow: No transition leads from the instance's status to the state named; details.allowed lists the states it can move to.
errors.commonCorrection: Read status, then name a state details.allowed lists, or move through one of them first.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance is already in the state the transition names.
errors.commonCorrection: Read status: the instance is already there, so nothing needs to move.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance is in a terminal state: no transition leaves it.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the work has ended. Create a new instance to start again.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance has no status to move from.
errors.commonCorrection: None: an instance without a status cannot move.

errors.description: Dependencies: A move into done while a blocker is open; details.details.blockers lists the open ones.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait for the open blockers to finish, or remove the ones the work goes on without, then try again.

tools.name: tasks_add_blocker
tools.title: tasks: addBlocker
tools.description: Makes another instance block this one. It must be of the type's own schema or one the config lists, exist, and not be blocked by this instance, directly or through others. An instance in a gated state that is terminal takes no blocker that is not finished.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

schema.description: The blocker's schema; the instance's own when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to make an instance of tasks or documents (the instance's own schema when schema is absent) block this one. It holds up the transition into done until it finishes.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use at create; give the blockers in behaviors.Dependencies.blockers instead.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the blocker, with its status and whether it is open; blocked is true while one is.

errors.description: Dependencies: addBlocker, or a create's blockers, naming an instance that already blocks this one.
errors.commonCorrection: Leave it: that instance already blocks this one.

errors.description: Dependencies: addBlocker, or a create's blockers, giving an edge that would close a cycle.
errors.commonCorrection: Remove the edge that makes the other instance wait on this one first, or leave this edge out.

errors.description: Dependencies: addBlocker, or a create's blockers, giving an open blocker while the instance is in a gated state no transition leaves.
errors.commonCorrection: Add only finished blockers to an instance in a gated state no transition leaves, or none.

tools.name: tasks_remove_blocker
tools.title: tasks: removeBlocker
tools.description: Stops another instance from blocking this one.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

schema.description: The blocker's schema; the instance's own when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to stop an instance blocking this one, as when a blocker failed or was cancelled and the work goes on without it.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the blocker it removed; blocked is false once no open blocker is left.

tools.name: tasks_list_blockers
tools.title: tasks: listBlockers
tools.description: Lists the instance's blockers in the order they were added, one page at a time, with each one's status and whether it blocks.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many blockers; 50 when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read the instance's blockers, each with its status and whether it is open.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: tasks_list_dependents
tools.title: tasks: listDependents
tools.description: Lists the instances this one blocks, of every schema the caller may read, in the order they were added, one page at a time.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many dependents; 50 when absent. A page holds fewer when the caller may not read some of their schemas.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read the instances this one blocks, in schemas the caller may read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: tasks_link
tools.title: tasks: link
tools.description: Points a link at an instance of its schema, replacing the target it had; a many-valued link adds the instance to its list, or pins again one it holds. A pinned link records the target's latest revision or release, or the one given.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

name.description: The link's name in the config.

release.description: For a link pinned to a release, the target's release to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

revision.description: For a link pinned to a revision, the target's revision to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to point parent, project or spec at an instance of its schema, moving it when it is set. spec records the target's latest revision, or the one given.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use at create; give the links in behaviors.Links instead.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the link: its name, schema, id and the revision or release a pinned link records.

errors.description: Links: A link pinned to a revision, by link or a create's links, to a target that has no revision to pin yet.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait until the target has a revision, or link a target that has one.

tools.name: tasks_unlink
tools.title: tasks: unlink
tools.description: Clears an optional link, or removes one target of a many-valued link. A required link cannot be unlinked, only moved, and a required many-valued link keeps at least one target.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

id.description: The target to remove, which a many-valued link needs; for a link that holds one target, the one it must hold.

name.description: The link's name in the config.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to clear parent or spec.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on project: a required link is moved with link, never unlinked.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the link as it was.

errors.description: Links: unlink of a required link, which link moves and nothing unlinks, or of the last target of a required many-valued link.
errors.commonCorrection: Move the link with link instead.

tools.name: tasks_list_linked
tools.title: tasks: listLinked
tools.description: Lists the instances of this schema whose link points at an instance, in the order the links were made, one page at a time; for a pinned link, with the revision or the release each records, the target's latest and whether the target has moved past it.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

name.description: The link's name in the config.

stale.description: Only the pinned links whose target has moved past the revision or the release they record.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to find the Task instances whose link points at a target. With stale true, only the pinned ones the target has moved past.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: comments_inbox
tools.title: Comments: inbox
tools.description: The caller's inbox across every schema of the namespace that composes Comments and that the caller may read, newest first: the messages that mention it, the threads it follows that have replies of others, and the conversations it has read that have top-level messages of others. Each item names the latest such message and how many of them the caller has not read; an item with none unread is done. A mention is read once the caller's marker on the conversation, for a top-level message, or on its thread, for a reply, passes it. Mentions reach back as far as the config's deliveryRetentionMs.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

kinds.description: The kinds of item to list; every kind when absent.

limit.description: At most this many items; 50 when absent.

unread.description: true lists only items with unread messages, false only done ones; both when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to call Comments's inbox across every schema of this namespace that composes Comments: The caller's inbox across every schema of the namespace that composes Comments and that the caller may read, newest first: the messages that mention it, the threads it follows that have replies of others, and the conversations it has read that have top-level messages of others. Each item names the latest such message and how many of them the caller has not read; an item with none unread is done. A mention is read once the caller's marker on the conversation, for a top-level message, or on its thread, for a reply, passes it. Mentions reach back as far as the config's deliveryRetentionMs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use for one instance or one schema's instances; call that schema's operations of Comments.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the operation's result, over the schemas the caller may read.

tools.name: comments_search_messages
tools.title: Comments: searchMessages
tools.description: Searches the bodies of the posted and interrupted messages of every schema of the namespace that composes Comments and that the caller may read, best match first: a message is found when its body holds each word of query, in any order, case and diacritics aside. schema narrows the search to one type, instanceId to one conversation, and thread to one thread, its top-level message and its replies. A composing message's draft, a deleted message and the text before an edit are never found. The order is each database's own ranking, bm25 on SQLite and ts_rank_cd on Postgres, so the two may order the same hits differently; a search reaches its first 1000 hits.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

instanceId.description: Only messages of this instance's conversation; needs schema.

limit.description: At most this many hits; 50 when absent.

query.description: The words to find, plain text split at white space: quotes, AND, OR, NOT, NEAR and * are words like any other. The first 8 words count.

schema.description: Only messages on instances of this schema; nothing is found when the caller may not read it.

thread.description: Only the thread of this top-level message: it and its replies; needs instanceId.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to call Comments's searchMessages across every schema of this namespace that composes Comments: Searches the bodies of the posted and interrupted messages of every schema of the namespace that composes Comments and that the caller may read, best match first: a message is found when its body holds each word of query, in any order, case and diacritics aside. schema narrows the search to one type, instanceId to one conversation, and thread to one thread, its top-level message and its replies. A composing message's draft, a deleted message and the text before an edit are never found. The order is each database's own ranking, bm25 on SQLite and ts_rank_cd on Postgres, so the two may order the same hits differently; a search reaches its first 1000 hits.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use for one instance or one schema's instances; call that schema's operations of Comments.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the operation's result, over the schemas the caller may read.

tools.name: comments_claim_deliveries
tools.title: Comments: claimDeliveries
tools.description: Claims deliveries that are due, at most limit, oldest due first, under one new token that lapses after ttlMs, so two notifiers never send one twice: each pending one, each failed one whose next attempt has come, and each claimed one whose claim lapsed. Only deliveries of schemas the caller may read whose config names a deliverPermission the caller holds; with subjects or prefix, only theirs. A due delivery whose message no longer stands, or whose subject has read it, is dropped and not returned. Each delivery carries what a notifier needs to act with no other read.

limit.description: At most this many deliveries; 20 when absent.

prefix.description: Only deliveries to subjects that start with it, agent: say; not with subjects.

ttlMs.description: How long the claim holds, in milliseconds; 60000 when absent. A delivery not settled by then is due again.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to call Comments's claimDeliveries across every schema of this namespace that composes Comments: Claims deliveries that are due, at most limit, oldest due first, under one new token that lapses after ttlMs, so two notifiers never send one twice: each pending one, each failed one whose next attempt has come, and each claimed one whose claim lapsed. Only deliveries of schemas the caller may read whose config names a deliverPermission the caller holds; with subjects or prefix, only theirs. A due delivery whose message no longer stands, or whose subject has read it, is dropped and not returned. Each delivery carries what a notifier needs to act with no other read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use for one instance or one schema's instances; call that schema's operations of Comments.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the operation's result, over the schemas the caller may read.

tools.name: comments_settle_deliveries
tools.title: Comments: settleDeliveries
tools.description: Settles deliveries the caller claimed under token: sent; failed, which makes each due again after a backoff until the config's maxAttempts claims, then drops it; or dropped. Needs the deliverPermission of each delivery's schema. Every id must be held under the token, or nothing is settled.

error.description: Why it failed or was dropped, kept on the delivery; not with sent.

ids.description: The ids of the deliveries to settle.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to call Comments's settleDeliveries across every schema of this namespace that composes Comments: Settles deliveries the caller claimed under token: sent; failed, which makes each due again after a backoff until the config's maxAttempts claims, then drops it; or dropped. Needs the deliverPermission of each delivery's schema. Every id must be held under the token, or nothing is settled.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use for one instance or one schema's instances; call that schema's operations of Comments.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the operation's result, over the schemas the caller may read.

cases.name: initialize > answers the engine as the server, with tools, on the 2025 revision the client asks for
initialize > negotiates the 2026-07-28 revision with a client that probes for it

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.title: List schemas
tools.description: Lists the schemas this namespace reaches, its own and the shared namespace's, with each one's live version and whether it has a draft.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn which schemas this namespace reaches and which of them have a live version.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's fields or operations; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each schema's name, its live version and whether it has a draft.

tools.name: describe_schema
tools.title: Describe a schema
tools.description: Returns a schema's describe document: how a UI shows an instance (its display, and each field's title and icon), the JSON Schema of an instance, the behaviors its type composes with their config, and every operation with its parameters, its result and its tool.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before calling a schema's tools: it gives the JSON Schema of an instance, each behavior with its config and summary, and each operation with its parameters, result and guidance.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read instances; call the schema's get or list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the describe document of the live version.

tools.name: define_schema
tools.title: Define a schema draft
tools.description: Stores a schema-file document (the form superschematic format --to=json writes) as the draft of its name, replacing the draft before it. It does not publish: a draft goes live only through the HTTP publish route.

document.description: The schema-file document: kind General, a name, and the types; superschematic format --to=json writes it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to store a schema-file document as the draft of its name, replacing the draft before it.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to publish: a draft goes live only through the HTTP publish route.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the draft, with its name and hash; the live version is unchanged.

tools.name: list_behaviors
tools.title: List behaviors
tools.description: Lists the behaviors this engine runs, which a schema's types may compose: each one's name and description, the behaviors it requires and conflicts with, and the fields and operations it adds.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before composing behaviors in a draft, to learn which behaviors this engine runs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's config of its behaviors; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each behavior's name, description, requirements, conflicts, fields and operations.

tools.name: describe_behavior
tools.title: Describe a behavior
tools.description: Returns a behavior's declaration: the JSON Schema of the config a type gives it, of the parameters a create gives it and of the entry a write's preconditions carry for it, the behaviors it requires and conflicts with, its fields, its operations with their scope, parameters, result and invocation policy, and the codes its vetoes carry.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn what a behavior takes before composing it: its config, its create parameters, its preconditions and the codes its vetoes carry.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's config of the behavior; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the behavior's declaration, with its defaults filled in.

tools.name: get_value
tools.title: Get a stored value
tools.description: Returns a value the engine stores by its hash, { hash, bytes, value }: a field whose JSON is longer than the engine's threshold, which an event (and an instance read with valueRefs) carries as a ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }. The caller must be able to read a schema of this namespace whose instances, events or behaviors hold the value.

hash.description: The value's hash: the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON, as a ref's $value holds it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read a large field an event, or an instance read with valueRefs, carries as a ref ({ "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }), by its hash.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read an instance; call its schema's get, which returns every field inline unless valueRefs asks for refs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the value with its hash and its size in bytes.

tools.name: list_namespaces
tools.title: List namespaces
tools.description: Lists the namespaces the caller may see: each one's name, whether the engine's options configure it or a create made it, whether it is the shared namespace, and whether it is archived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn which namespaces you may see, and whether each is archived.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to list a namespace's schemas; call list_schemas.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each namespace's name, origin (configured by the engine's options, or created), whether it is the shared namespace, and its state (active or archived).

tools.name: create_namespace
tools.title: Create a namespace
tools.description: Creates a namespace, which holds schemas and instances of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself. Its name is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to make a namespace for a new project: it starts with no schemas of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to make a schema; call define_schema in the namespace. Do not use for a name that is a namespace already, archived or not: the create is refused (conflict).
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, active, with who made it and when.

tools.name: archive_namespace
tools.title: Archive a namespace
tools.description: Archives a namespace a create made: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, and it refuses every write, and runs no reaction or schedule, until it is unarchived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when a project made with create_namespace is finished: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, every write is refused (namespace_archived), and its reactions and schedules stop.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on a namespace the engine's options configure, which is refused (conflict), or to remove data: nothing is removed.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, archived, with who archived it and when; archiving an archived namespace changes nothing.

tools.name: unarchive_namespace
tools.title: Unarchive a namespace
tools.description: Lets an archived namespace be written again; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to write again to an archived namespace.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on an active namespace, which stays as it is.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, active; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

tools.name: item_create
tools.title: Create Item
tools.description: Creates a Item: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Item: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: item_get
tools.title: Get Item
tools.description: Returns the Item with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Item to read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Item instances; call list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance with its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: item_list
tools.title: List Item
tools.description: Lists Item instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

cursor.description: The previous page's next

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Item instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's.

tools.name: review_move_anchor
tools.title: Review: moveAnchor
tools.description: Moves a code block of a posted or interrupted message to the same code at another revision, where a caller that knows the repository found it, a git extension after a push say: the block takes revision and lines and keeps its snippet, and records the anchor it was first given with as original, how many times it moved, and who moved it last and when; each move's event holds the steps between. It is not an edit: the message's text, editedAt, edits and edit window are untouched. Its author may move it; another caller needs the config's anchorPermission or moderatePermission.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

block.description: The code block's index in the message's blocks, from 0.

lines.description: The first and the last line of the same code at that revision, counted from 1, both included; the first is at most the last.

revision.description: The revision the code is at now: a commit's id, as the repository names it.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to move a code block of a posted or interrupted message to the same code at another revision, once the caller has found where it went (after a push, say): the block takes revision and lines, keeps its snippet, and records its first anchor as original and its moves; its author may move it. It is not an edit: the body, editedAt, edits and the edit window are untouched. It is beside the instance: the instance's seq and ETag do not move, and a lease held by another does not stop it.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change what a code block quotes; edit the message.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the record, the block moved.

tools.name: item_update
tools.title: Update Item
tools.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the Item with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Item

preconditions.description: Preconditions by behavior: each entry is checked against its behavior's schema and handed to its guard, which refuses the call when it does not hold

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Item with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

tools.name: item_delete
tools.title: Delete Item
tools.description: Deletes the Item with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

preconditions.description: Preconditions by behavior: each entry is checked against its behavior's schema and handed to its guard, which refuses the call when it does not hold

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Item with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

expect.name: Approvals
expect.description: Sign-offs that gate states of the type's Workflow. A transition into a gated state, from a state its gate allows, waits until as many distinct principals holding the gate's permission as its count have signed off; the instance's creator cannot sign unless the gate allows it. A change of the instance's own fields consumes every gate's sign-offs, unless the config keeps them, and entering a gated state consumes that gate's, so a return to it signs again. Consumed sign-offs stay listed. Deleting the instance deletes its sign-offs.

expect.name: Branches
expect.description: Makes each instance the root of a version graph: refs, a primary line and drafts of it, over rows of the kinds the config names, each kind's content a type of the schema document; commits, merges, rebases and reverts; and a release pointer whose history is the release log, its version the release field. The instance's own fields stay outside the graph. The graph lives in the behavior's own tables, and deleting the instance deletes it. With sweep in its config, a schedule discards idle drafts and keeps the graph's storage in bounds.

expect.name: Comments
expect.description: A conversation on the instance: messages, each top-level or a reply in the thread of a top-level one, one level deep, which their authors edit and delete, others react to and pin, and whose threads are resolved and reopened. A message may be streamed as it is written: begin holds its place as composing, appendDraft adds to its draft and sends the draft signal to the streams open on the instance, and finish posts it; one whose author stops appending for composeTimeoutMs is interrupted, keeping what was written. Readers send typing and viewing, signals the engine delivers and does not keep. Each caller has a read marker on the conversation and on each thread, which markRead moves, and follows the threads it posts in, is mentioned in, or follows with follow. Each message that comes to stand, and each edit that adds a mention, records a delivery for each subject it mentions and each follower of its thread but its author, which a notifier or an agent dispatcher outside the engine claims and settles with claimDeliveries and settleDeliveries; the engine sends nothing. inbox reads a caller's mentions, followed threads and read conversations across every schema of the namespace it may read, and searchMessages searches the bodies of the messages that stand. A message written by an agent or a service acting for someone records that subject as for: the subject follows its thread and hears of it from no delivery, as its author does, while its author, the caller, is the one whose read markers, follows, reactions and drafts it writes; acting for someone grants nothing an author or a permission holder may do. Besides ref and action blocks, a message may hold code blocks, a place in code at a revision with the text captured when it was posted, which moveAnchor moves to the same code at a newer revision, and attachment blocks, the description of a file the deployment stores. Every writing operation on an instance is beside the instance: it writes Comments' own tables, never moves the instance's seq, ETag or updatedAt, and runs none of its guards, so a lease on the instance does not stop a reply. A caller who may read the instance reads the conversation; the policy is asked write for a writing operation, post included. Deleting the instance deletes its conversation, with its read markers, follows, deliveries and search index.

expect.name: Constants
expect.description: Fields of the type that its create sets and nothing changes after: an update that changes one, a caller's or one a behavior's operation applies, is refused at the field, unless the caller holds the config's permission. A field the create leaves absent stays absent. What routes an instance, such as a step's kind or the key a blueprint stamped it with, stays what its create gave it.

expect.name: Dependencies
expect.description: Blockers between instances. A blocker is finished once its status is a terminal state of its own schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts, a success by default. An instance is blocked while a blocker is not finished, and a transition of its own Workflow into a gated state waits until none blocks it. A blocker is an instance of the type's own schema, or of a schema the config lists, that composes Workflow; an edge that would close a cycle is refused. A create may give its blockers. Deleting a blocker removes its edges.

expect.name: Derived
expect.description: Own fields a model outside the engine fills from other own fields, under an instruction the schema holds (D73). The engine calls no model: a deriver holding the config's permission pulls the stale fields with staleDerivations (each one's inputs, instruction, model label and the field's JSON Schema, which is the output's) and settles its answers with settleDerivations, presenting the hash it pulled. A value is written with the operation's update(), so the type's validation and every guard judge it, and its event attributes it to Derived with the confidence given. A field is stale when its inputs, instruction, model or type moved since its last value; that value stays until a new one settles. Once a caller, or another behavior's operation, writes a derived field, Derived stops deriving it until rederive. A failure appends no event; after maxAttempts the field waits until its inputs move. Deleting the instance deletes what Derived keeps of it.

expect.name: Links
expect.description: Named links from the instance to instances of the schemas its config names, set by link or given at create: each holds one target, or with many a list of them. A pinned link records the target's revision (its schema composes Revisions) or its release (its schema composes Branches), and reports the target's latest beside it and whether the target has moved past it. A required link is given at create, can be moved to another target but not unlinked, and the delete of its target is refused; a required many-valued link keeps at least one target, and only its last target's delete is refused. A deleted target leaves every link that holds it.

expect.name: Numbering
expect.description: A number a person reads on each instance, set in its create's transaction from a count per namespace and schema: the format prints it, INV-{yyyy}-{seq:4} as INV-2026-0042. The count may run per target of a required, single-valued link and start again each UTC year, so a label is unique within its scope. A refused create takes no number; a delete leaves a gap. Nothing changes a number once set, and a list finds an instance by its label or its number. An instance made before its schema composed Numbering is numbered by assignNumber.

expect.name: Provenance
expect.description: Who set each own field last, and through what (D73): a caller's create or update, or the behavior whose operation wrote it, with the confidence that operation attributed (D16, amended). With review, a write from the sources it names is proposed until a reviewer holding its permission accepts or rejects it, unless its confidence reaches below; a caller's write over a proposal makes it edited. A gate refuses a move of the type's Workflow into its state while a field it lists is proposed. Deleting the instance deletes its records.

expect.name: Reactions
expect.description: Rules that move Workflow statuses after a change commits: when the instance's status enters a state, when a field of the instance, its own or a behavior's, changes, when every instance that links to it through a link is in a terminal state, optionally one with a listed outcome, when one of them enters a terminal state with a listed outcome, when an all or any rollup of the instance comes to hold, or when the instance one of its links points to gains a revision or a release, move the instance, or the instance one of its links points to, to a state. An engine runs them after the commit, as the principal it names for its runner, so a rule never refuses the change that set it off. A target already in the state, with no transition to it, or whose guards refuse is left as it is.

expect.name: Revisions
expect.description: Immutable revisions of the instance's own fields: one when it is created and one each time they change, numbered 1, 2, 3, ..., read a page at a time or one by its number. With review in its config, a caller can propose a change as a merge patch, citing instances as evidence, and a caller who holds the review permission approves it, which applies the patch as an update, or rejects it; pendingProposals counts the proposals waiting. Deleting the instance deletes its revisions and proposals.

expect.name: Rollups
expect.description: Values derived from the instances that point at this one through a link of their schema's Links config: how many there are, how many hold each value of a field, the sum, least or greatest of a numeric field, a field's value on the one created last, and whether every one or some one is in a terminal state of its schema's Workflow, optionally one with a listed outcome. A value is computed when the instance is read, as the caller, from at most 500 linked instances; a rollup over more has none. A rollup of every or some one may gate states of the type's Workflow: a transition into one waits until the rollup holds.

expect.name: Search
expect.description: Full-text search over the instance's own text fields, which the config names, and with vectors in the config, vector search over embeddings an outside embedder computes from the same text. The index is kept in the transaction of each create, update and delete; an embedder pulls the instances whose text changed since their vector was computed (staleEmbeddings) and settles their vectors back (settleEmbeddings). The schema-level search returns the matching ids in rank order, by the text, by a vector the caller gives, or by both fused, from the instances of the caller's namespace only, and similar returns the instances nearest to one, or to a draft's text.

expect.name: StateRules
expect.description: Rules per state of the type's Workflow: the own fields an instance must hold to enter a state, and the ones that cannot change while it is in it. A field is held when it is neither absent nor null. A transition into a state while a field it requires is not held is vetoed, and a create whose initial state requires one is refused at the field. An update, a caller's or one a behavior's operation applies, that clears a field the instance's state requires, or changes one it freezes, is vetoed; a caller with the config's permission may change a frozen field. Requires Workflow.

expect.name: Timers
expect.description: Named deadlines on the instance, each due a time after it starts: at the create, each time the status of the type's Workflow enters a state, or at the time a date-time field of the instance holds, before it with a negative offset. A due deadline fires once: it is marked fired and can move the status, from the state it starts in unless the config names others, whatever the move meets. A change of the status can cancel a pending deadline, and a field deadline moves with its field. The engine's runner fires the due deadlines every sweepMs; a caller with the config's permission resets or snoozes one. A deadline that names a state needs Workflow on the type.

expect.name: Workflow
expect.description: A state machine on the instance: a status that starts in the initial state and changes only through transition, along a transition the config lists. A transition may name a permission the caller must hold. A state that no transition leaves is terminal, and a terminal state has an outcome: success, failure or neutral, success unless the config says otherwise. Other instances' blockers, rollups and reactions read it.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.title: notes: search
tools.description: Searches the schema's instances in the caller's namespace and returns the matching ids, best match first, one page at a time: by query, by vector, or by both, whose rankings are fused. A query is plain words by default: an instance matches when its indexed fields hold every word, and quotes and operators in the query are text. With syntax fts5 the query is an SQLite FTS5 expression (phrases, AND, OR, NOT, NEAR, prefix*), without column filters. A vector, computed with the config's model from the text to search for, ranks the instances whose vectors are settled by cosine similarity. With a vector, each hit says how it matched.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; refused when it is not the config's.

query.description: What to search for, as text.

vector.description: The vector to search for: as many numbers as the config's dimensions, computed with its model.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to find Note instances by words in title or body: plain words match when the fields hold every one; syntax fts5 takes an FTS5 expression. A vector of 384 numbers from model minilm-l6 ranks by similarity, alone or fused with a query.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to page through every instance; call list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns hits best first, each its id, rank and a snippet of the field that matched. Pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

Given text in place of an id, the text of an instance not yet created, it ranks the same way by that text and the vector given with it, if any. Call it before creating an instance, to find near-duplicates to reuse or link instead.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

id.description: The instance whose neighbours to list.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; refused when it is not the config's.

text.description: In place of id, the text of an instance not yet created: its indexed fields that hold more than whitespace, in the config's order, joined by a blank line, as an embedder is given an instance's.

vector.description: With text, the text's vector: as many numbers as the config's dimensions, computed with its model.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before creating a Note, to find near-duplicates to reuse or link instead: with id, the instances nearest to one you have; with text, the ones nearest to a draft's title and body, joined by a blank line. With text, a vector of 384 numbers from model minilm-l6 computed from the same text ranks by similarity too.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to search by a few words; call search.

tools.name: notes_settle_embeddings
tools.title: notes: settleEmbeddings
tools.description: Stores the vectors an embedder computed from the text staleEmbeddings returned, each with the hash it returned with it. An item whose instance is gone, or whose text or model changed since, is skipped. A vector of the wrong dimensions, all zeros, or with a value a 32-bit float cannot hold refuses the whole batch. Needs vectors in the config and the permission it names. Appends no event: a vector is derived from text the log records, and no read of an instance shows it.

superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns how many it settled and each skipped item with its reason, moved or not_found.
